title: Implement fractional capacity credits and per-tenant isolation operator
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Summary:
During the 2026-02-26 capacity incident many Dedicated clusters experienced a region-wide throughput collapse driven by a small number of tenants exhausting burst credits and causing KV cache churn. P99 latency climbed from ~120ms to 2.4s and we observed automated reservation scale-ups followed by eviction storms. Root cause elements we identified: (1) coarse-grained reservation sizing that did not reflect multi-tenant burst patterns, (2) a zero-sum burst refill that allowed single tenants to consume sustained short-term extra capacity, and (3) no fast soft-isolation path to limit a tenant’s refill rate before evictions began.

Proposal:
Implement a new lightweight "fractional capacity credits" system and a per-tenant isolation operator in the control plane/runtime that accomplishes three goals: 1) allow fractional (sub-unit) reservation accounting so we can represent realistic customer reservations and spare fractional credits for bursts, 2) detect and apply a graduated soft-isolate (throttle refill and batch priority demotion) against noisy tenants before hard eviction, and 3) expose a small set of metrics to customers and SREs to make decisions clear (credit-burn-rate, refill-rate, burst-debt). The operator lives in the Dedicated control plane, reconciles tenant credit balances, and emits decisions that the runtime enforces via token bucket refill modulation and batch admission hints.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Fractional credits increase accounting precision and allow gradual redistributions, but add complexity to billing and telemetry and a rounding policy needs to be defined (we propose micro-credit units of 0.01 GPU-second).
- Soft-isolation avoids noisy-tenant evictions (better customer experience) but requires careful thresholds to avoid starving legitimate short bursts. We'll gate thresholds behind a feature flag and conservative defaults.
- We deliberately avoid a hard-eviction-first strategy; hard ejects will remain a last-resort escape hatch for severe SLA violations.

Telemetry findings that motivated changes:
- Top 5 tenants during the incident consumed 62% of burst budget in 12 minutes.
- Eviction rate spiked to 7x baseline during refill storms.
- Affected clusters showed KV cache miss-rate growth of +18pp correlated with refill storms.

Planned implementation steps:
1. Prototype fractional credit accounting in the allocator (runtime change) and a control plane operator to maintain balances. (owner: Liam)
2. Implement a soft-isolate policy: dynamic refill dampening + batch admission score penalty. (owner: Runtime team)
3. Add three telemetry signals (credit-burn-rate, burst-debt, soft-isolate-actions) and surface in Console. (owner: Observability)
4. Canary rollout to one Dedicated pool with conservative limits, 48h monitoring window and automatic rollback on P99 regression >20%.
5. Post-canary audit and incremental ramp to remaining pools.

Acceptance criteria:
- Canary shows no >20% P99 regression and reduces eviction rate by >=40% for noisy scenarios in synthetic tests.
- Console displays per-tenant credit-burn-rate and soft-isolate history.
- Billing team approves rounding policy for fractional credits.

Links to artifacts:
- Incident writeup: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/INC-2026-02-26-capacity-event
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood/realtime/pull/4218
- Operator design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/FRAC-CREDITS-DESIGN
- Synthetic test harness: https://grafana.redwood.net/d/ops/synthetic-capacity-tests

Longer term:
If this prototype succeeds we will fold fractional credits into pricing docs and add a tenant-facing quota dashboard. The operator could also be extended to support multi-cluster credit migration in regions with chronic skew.
